laterChanges: Act 174 of the 2026 Fiscal Session raises the cap to $675 beginning with assessment year 2026, normally collected in 2027. It does not replace the $600 cap for assessment year 2025.
name: Arkansas
overview: The homestead credit reduces qualifying homeowners' property-tax liability without an income test.

programs.name: Homestead Property Tax Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: Lesser of $600 and qualifying homestead tax for assessment year 2025, normally collected in 2026.
programs.formulaSummary: Nonrefundable bill credit equal to the lesser of qualified homestead real-property ad valorem tax before this credit and the assessment-year cap. Any unused cap is not a cash payment.
programs.application: Register the homestead and establish eligibility with the county assessor.
eligibilityNotes: Applies to a qualifying owner-occupied homestead.
Assessment year and bill-payment year differ; the assessment-year cap governs even if payment is early or late.

Actual county parcel qualification, valid registration, annual property history and qualified pre-credit tax must be established; current owner tenure or generic tax paid alone does not establish the credit.
interactions: Assessment limitations and disability/veteran exemptions are separate forms of relief.
A person claiming the disabled-veteran property-tax exemption cannot also claim this credit; veteran status alone is not the exclusion.

researchNotes: DFA confirms Act 330 of 2025 increased the credit; the fiscal statement specifies 2025 assessment-year applicability.
Do not substitute a 2025 cash-payment comparison for the 2025 assessment-year credit. Assessment 2025 normally appears on the 2026 bill; assessment 2026 normally appears on the 2027 bill.

Verified recent cap history is $425 for assessment 2023, $500 for assessment 2024, $600 for assessment 2025 and $675 from assessment 2026. A tax paid during 2025 ordinarily relates to assessment 2024 and its $500 cap.

County-confirmed parcel and claim facts are required. Unknown liability, registration or property history is not a verified zero award, and initial source-pass completion does not validate a household calculation.
